chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan, who said:
I heard a man saying to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding al-nabeez? For Abu Maryam drinks it, and he claims that you have ordered with its drinking.'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Far be it from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that I should order with the drinking of an intoxicant. By Allah, it is something for which I fear the authorities, and nothing else.'
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is prohibited, therefore whatever a lot of it were to intoxicate, so a little of it is prohibited.'

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabeez (a specific type of fermented drink made from dates or raisins)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the prohibition of nabeez and the fear of authorities in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between absolute prohibition (haram) and precautionary avoidance (takhayyur) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam al-Sadiq (as) avoided 'al-nabeez' not due to intrinsic impurity but to prevent conflict with the Umayyad authorities who enforced its ban. It reinforces the foundational principle of 'kathiruhu wa qaliluhu haram' (much and little are both forbidden), linking the specific ruling on fermented date/water drinks to the broader Prophetic maxim that any substance causing intoxication in large quantities is prohibited even in small amounts.
